plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. It is a classic winter bloomer in mild climates and is widely cultivated in gardens and parks, with thousands of cultivars.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (December to April in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant used to make all true teas, including green, black, and oolong.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant blossoms on bare branches in the coldest part of winter. It is celebrated in East Asian art and poetry as a symbol of perseverance and the coming spring.
plants.location: Native to southern China; widely grown in Japan, Korea, and Taiwan, and in temperate gardens elsewhere
plants.funFact: The blossoms often open while snow is still on the ground, which is why the tree is one of the 'Three Friends of Winter' in Chinese culture.

plants.name: Hippeastrum hybrids
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with huge trumpet-shaped flowers on tall hollow stalks. In the Northern Hemisphere it is commonly forced indoors for winter blooms, while in the Southern Hemisphere it blooms outdoors in summer gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter indoors in the Northern Hemisphere; late spring to summer outdoors in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America and the Andes; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Amaryllis bulbs can bloom again year after year, and a single bulb may produce several flower stalks in a season.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and rounded umbels of blue trumpet-shaped flowers on tall stems. It thrives in the warm summer conditions of the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (December to February in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South Africa; naturalized and widely planted in Australia, New Zealand, and coastal California
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it is not a true lily, and the genus name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower'.
